about: Claim-to-source record for the M5 Guardian website. Every factual statement the page makes about the device is listed with the website file that says it and a verbatim quotation from a repository file that supports it. Paths are relative to the repository root (sources) or to website/ (page). Status: current = what the device does now; host-only = validated by host tests, not on the device; deferred = not built yet. The page itself is a simulation: its moods, scenarios, names and counts are labelled demo or example values, not readings. lib/claims.test.ts checks that every page snippet and every quotation is still present.

claims.statement: Monitoring is receive-only; the stick transmits only for its phone setup access point and, as an ordinary Wi-Fi client, for its signed update check, and it does not join the network to monitor.

page.text: Receive-only monitoring: the stick transmits only for its phone setup access point and, as an ordinary Wi-Fi client, for its signed update check.
Guardian listens on its 2.4 GHz channel, without joining it to monitor.
RX-ONLY MONITOR
Receive-only Wi-Fi monitoring on the M5 StickS3.
receive-only monitoring

sources.quote: It is a detector. It listens and counts; the firmware has no raw-frame transmit call. It joins a network only as an ordinary client for its own signed update check, and raises a short-lived setup access point when you ask it to.
The password is needed only for the update check; the guarding itself never joins a network.

claims.statement: A stick with an update server stored stops listening for the seconds each update check takes, every 120 s by default; a stick installed from the website has no server and never checks by itself.

sources.quote: on a stick with an update server stored, by default every 120 s the stick stops listening for the seconds the check takes.
A stick without an update server (installed from the website) never checks by itself.
